correctness.rationale: For any non-overlapping weight-three code, distinct cyclic rotation orbits are full length n and disjoint, giving n|C| <= binomial(n,3). For the explicit h=ceil(n/3) construction, only prefixes ending at its first or second internal one could meet a suffix (all suffixes end 1). At the first, i_u+j_v >= n-1 precludes a sole terminal one; at the second, the suffix contains all three ones while the prefix contains exactly two. Exact summation over j gives the floor bound in each residue class mod 3, while counting periodic words gives the primitive-necklace transversal. Independent finite brute overlap/orbit comparisons n=4..16 and arithmetic tests n=4..100000 succeeded. No infinite premise relies on those tests.

value.rationale: Non-overlapping codes support unambiguous synchronization, and fixing Hamming weight models a strict pulse/composition budget. The result solves an exact maximum-cardinality problem for every blocklength, attaining a universal cyclic-volume bound even when nonprimitive necklaces exist. Its constructive perfect transversal for every primitive weight-three necklace exposes a structural saturation phenomenon, stronger than enumeration of finitely many cases and not a textbook substitution of unrestricted code size.
